_about: How the war cards' sides become entities of history.bin (Atlas v2 Phase 2d; docs/atlas-v2-design.md §7 'Phase 2d — as built'). READ by lib/war-resolve.js, which build-history.js (the extents), build-wars.js (atlas/data/wars.js) and the tests share. A side resolves in this order: (1) an entry under `sides` below; (2) the card's link in polity-spec.json / war-series.json (`links`: v for the victors, l for the losers); (3) the side's NAME is the label or key of one polity series; (4) its `keys` through `keyMap`; (5) its authored `area` stays an authored EXTENT (an entity of kind `extent`, drawn soft and said to be Folio's own approximation). Names of the card's keys that nothing resolves are listed as unresolved on wars.js, never drawn. `members`: a polity series key, with an optional [from, to] membership window (default: the war's own years, from the card) and the reason for the window. A window is a claim about when a state was in the war: each one below is a declaration, an invasion or an armistice, with the date in `why`; the entity is drawn only where its own steps (Cliopatria's rows) also lie. `keepExtent: true` keeps the card's authored area as well as the members. `ignoreKeys`: present-day names in a card's keys that name the same ground as a period key already resolved (Russia beside the Soviet Union, India beside the British Raj, Serbia and Croatia beside Yugoslavia, the Soviet republics): they are neither drawn nor listed as unresolved. `extentOnly`: skip the specs and keep the card's authored area (Cliopatria's Zhou begins in 1000 BCE, after the conquest of 1046 BCE).
